Subject: Severe latency spike impacting inference pipelines (Jun 1)

We're seeing sustained latency spikes across our production inference endpoints since ~08:40 PDT today. 95th percentile latency jumped from ~180ms to 1.8s and error-rate climbed to ~4% during peak. Impact: several downstream microservices are timing out and batch jobs are failing.

Attached is a short sample of client-side traces and the timestamped request ids (latency-sample-20270601.txt). Example request ids: req_20270601_0847_01, req_20270601_0852_14.

We need an urgent RCA and temporary mitigation — our board wants an exec readout today. Can you confirm you have a bridge and whether you can rollback any recent serving config?

Thanks,
Olivia Park

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike impacting inference pipelines (Jun 1)

On bridge and following the quick triage: initial root-cause hypothesis below.

Summary of technical findings (first-pass):
- Time window: 08:38-09:10 PDT.
- Observed: sudden KV cache eviction events on CT's dedicated inference pool coincident with a large short burst of long-context requests (sequence length spiked from median 512 to 6k tokens).
- Effect: increased memory churn, more frequent context reloads, and higher per-token compute. This increased tail latency and pushed some workers over the error-rate threshold due to OOM/retries.
- Additional signal: a model-autoupdate window ran at 08:35 to roll forward a quantized variant (v2-q8) for lower-cost routing. The quantized path currently has a regression on very-long-context sequences leading to higher per-token execution time.

Immediate mitigations performed (10:00 PDT):
- Rolled back routing to the previous non-quantized variant for the affected model.
- Increased dedicated pool burst to +25% for the next 3 hours.
- Disabled automatic model-autoupdate for CT's project.

I'll attach a perf snapshot (perf-snapshot-ct-0602.png) and link to the metric slices in the ticket. Next steps: deeper profiling to confirm quantized-kernel regression vs kv-cache policy.

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Cobalt Therapeutics — Executive summary & mutual action plan

Olivia — following our bridge and the engineering analysis, here's the exec-facing summary and the mutual action plan. Attached: RCA packet draft (rca-packet-cobalt-20270604.pdf).

Executive summary (for your board):
- Incident: sustained latency and elevated errors on inference endpoints caused by an interaction between: (1) a short burst of very long-context requests that caused KV cache eviction, and (2) a regression in the newly deployed quantized execution path for long sequences.
- Customer impact: degraded 95th pct latency (180ms -> ~1.8s) and elevated 4% errors for a 30-minute window, causing downstream timeouts in internal pipelines.
- Actions taken: rollback to non-quantized variant, temporary capacity increase, disabled auto-updates.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) Short-term (within 72 hours) — Redwood:
   - Complete kernel-level profiling for quantized path on long contexts. Owner: Jonas. Due: 2027-06-03 EOD.
   - Validate KV cache eviction thresholds + adjust policy for CT workload. Owner: Infra. Due: 2027-06-03 EOD.
2) Customer collaboration — Cobalt:
   - Provide sample long-context request traces (Olivia). Due: 2027-06-02 noon.
3) Mid-term (2 weeks) — joint runbook and regression test: build a long-context perf test in our CI to prevent future regressions. Owner: Rishi + CT Eng. Due: 2027-06-17.
4) Business: Redwood to provide a one-time credit to offset incident impact (proposed 10% of June hosting invoice) subject to exec approval. Owner: Laura (to coordinate with Finance). Due: 2027-06-04.

Please confirm the MAP and whether you want an exec readout on Friday (2027-06-04) 09:00 PDT.

Thanks — Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
